literal: Even if forgotten, the Vedas acquiring is possible; (but) a Brahmin's birth status, when conduct slips, will be ruined.
translation: Even if he forgets the Vedas, a Brahmin can learn them again; but if his right conduct slips, his very birthright of high status is ruined.
modern: மறந்துபோனாலும் வேதத்தைக் கற்றுக்கொள்ள முடியும்; ஆனால், ஒரு பார்ப்பான் தன் ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறினால் அவனுடைய குடிப்பிறப்பின் உயர்வு அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of personal conduct over mere scriptural learning or birth status. The author uses the example of a Brahmin, whose traditional duty is to preserve and chant the Vedas. If such a person forgets the sacred texts, they can always be re-learned through effort. However, if he fails in his moral conduct, he loses his character, and his high birth status is instantly destroyed. Thus, character and conduct are far more fundamental and irreplaceable than rote knowledge or social lineage.
